families.name: Converging pointers over a symmetric string
families.idea: One pointer starts at each end and they walk toward each other, checking or repairing a mirror relationship between the characters they stand on. The invariant: everything outside the current pointer pair already satisfies the symmetry.
signals: asks whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards, possibly after limited edits
positions i and n-1-i are compared, swapped, or must correspond under some mapping
a small budget of deletions or moves to reach a palindrome-like state
families.trap: Building a reversed copy or checking substrings quadratically when one inward walk answers it — and in the 'one edit allowed' variants, greedily fixing only one side instead of trying both skip branches.
members: Minimum Number of Moves to Make Palindrome

families.name: Lockstep walk over two sequences
families.idea: Keep one index per sequence and advance them by simple local rules: on a match both move, on a mismatch exactly one moves. Because each pointer only ever moves forward, the whole comparison finishes in a single linear pass with no extra state.
signals: two strings or arrays compared, matched, or interleaved without any extra data structure
statement uses words like subsequence, abbreviation, version parts, or alternating merge
each input only needs to be read once, in order
families.trap: Reaching for edit-distance DP or materializing fully expanded strings when a forward (or backward) index walk with skip rules already decides the answer.
members: Append Characters to String to Make Subsequence

families.name: Slow writer, fast reader compaction
families.idea: A read pointer scans every element while a write pointer marks the boundary of finished output; elements worth keeping are copied down onto the write position. The invariant: everything left of the writer is exactly the final answer built so far.
signals: 'in place' plus remove, compact, dedupe, or move-to-front/back on an array
the answer is the same array with some elements dropped or shifted, plus a new length
O(1) extra space is demanded
families.trap: Deleting elements one at a time or building a second array, which turns one O(n) pass into O(n^2) time or O(n) space and misses the point of the writer boundary.

families.name: Pivot, swap, reverse: the next arrangement
families.idea: To produce the next-larger arrangement of the same elements, scan from the right for the first position that can still grow (the pivot), swap in the smallest larger candidate from the suffix, then reverse the suffix so the tail is as small as possible.
signals: asks for the next bigger or smaller number/permutation using exactly the same digits or elements
rearrangement with a lexicographic ordering requirement
must be done in place, ruling out enumerating permutations
families.trap: Trying to enumerate or sort permutations — the answer is fully determined by the rightmost descent, and everything beyond that local repair is wasted work.

families.name: Reordering by composing block reversals
families.idea: A reversal keeps every element but flips a block's order, so the right sequence of block reversals produces rotations and word reorderings entirely in place: reverse the whole, then reverse each piece (or the other way around).
signals: rotate or shift an array by k positions with O(1) extra space
reverse the order of words or segments while keeping their insides intact
output is a block-level rearrangement of the input
families.trap: Moving elements one step at a time k times, or splitting into temporary buffers, when two or three reversals achieve the same rearrangement in place.

families.name: Two runners separated by a controlled gap
families.idea: Launch a second pointer at a fixed offset from the first, or route two pointers over paths of equal total length, so that when one reaches a known endpoint the other stands exactly on the target. Distance bookkeeping replaces a second pass.
signals: kth-from-the-end of a singly linked structure with no length given
find the node where two chains or upward paths meet
only forward traversal exists and a one-pass solution is hinted at
families.trap: Measuring the length first and doing arithmetic in a second pass — correct, but misses the one-pass alignment; the classic bug is an off-by-one when setting up the gap.
members: Remove nth Node from End of List
Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree III

families.name: Tortoise and hare cycle detection
families.idea: Two pointers move at speeds one and two through a chain of 'next' steps; if the chain ever loops, the fast pointer must lap the slow one inside the loop, so a meeting proves a cycle. It works on any deterministic successor function, not just linked lists.
signals: asks whether a process repeats forever or whether a structure contains a cycle
every state has exactly one successor: a next node, a digit function, or an index jump
O(1) space is required where a visited-set would be the obvious answer
families.trap: Reaching for a visited hash set — fine for correctness, but it spends O(n) space the problem exists to eliminate, and it breaks when states cannot be stored or the input must not be mutated.

families.name: Fast pointer finds the middle
families.idea: While the fast pointer takes two steps for every one of the slow pointer's, the slow pointer lands on the midpoint the moment the fast one runs off the end — splitting a list of unknown length in one pass. Most members then reverse or rewire one of the halves.
signals: middle of a linked list, or the first half compared against the second
pairs of nodes mirrored around the center, like i and n-1-i twins
splitting a list into halves when its length is not given
families.trap: Copying node values into an array to index freely — it works, but silently abandons the O(1)-space constraint that the half-and-reverse composition is designed to satisfy.
members: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List

families.name: Every value has a home index
families.idea: When values come from a bounded range like 1..n, index i can serve as the parking spot for value i: keep swapping each element toward its home slot until every position holds its own value or a proven stranger. Whatever ends up out of place is the answer — the missing, duplicated, or first-absent value.
signals: an array of n numbers drawn from a bounded range such as 0..n or 1..n
asks for missing, duplicated, or first-absent values
O(n) time with O(1) extra space is demanded, ruling out sorting and hash sets
families.trap: Sorting or building a hash set — both pass, but both ignore that the value range itself is the index space the problem handed you for free.
members: Find the First K Missing Positive Numbers

families.name: Reversing links with a three-pointer walk
families.idea: Walk the list carrying prev and curr, flipping each node's next backwards as you pass; windowed variants apply the same flip inside a bounded group and then stitch the group's ends to its neighbors. All the real difficulty lives in the stitching, because a reversed window's old head becomes its new tail.
signals: reverse a whole linked list, a sublist between two positions, or every group of k nodes
in-place / O(1)-space requirement on a linked list
output order is the input order with some segments flipped
families.trap: Copying values into an array to reverse them, and in windowed versions, losing the boundary node that must reconnect the reversed group to the rest of the list.
members: Reverse Nodes In Even Length Groups

families.name: Deleting by rewiring past the node
families.idea: Nothing is ever really deleted — the predecessor's next pointer is redirected to skip the unwanted node or run of nodes. A dummy node in front of the head makes the head deletable by the same rule as everything else.
signals: remove every node matching a value or condition from a linked list
drop duplicates from an already-sorted list
keep-M-skip-N style retention patterns
families.trap: Forgetting the head itself can be removed (no dummy node), or advancing immediately after one unlink so a run of consecutive removals slips through.
members: Delete N Nodes After M Nodes of a Linked List

families.name: Cutting and re-splicing whole segments
families.idea: Rearrange the list by locating a few seam nodes, cutting there, and reconnecting entire chains with a constant number of pointer writes — no node is copied or moved, only next pointers are redirected. Closing the list into a ring first often turns 'rotate' into nothing more than 'choose where to cut'.
signals: rotate, split, or regroup a linked list at the segment level rather than value level
output contains the same nodes re-blocked: odd/even positions, k parts, folded halves
circular lists, or an answer defined by a position like k mod n
families.trap: Simulating the movement node by node — rotating one step k times, or rebuilding with fresh nodes — when computing the seam position does the whole job with O(1) pointer changes.
members: Insert into a Sorted Circular Linked List

families.name: Grow-and-shrink: longest valid window
families.idea: Expand the right edge one step at a time; whenever the window breaks the constraint, advance the left edge just enough to restore it. Both edges only move forward, so the longest valid window falls out of one linear pass.
signals: asks for the longest contiguous substring/subarray satisfying a constraint
adding elements can only break the constraint, removing can only repair it
phrases like 'at most k distinct', 'at most k flips', 'within a budget'
families.trap: If shrinking the window does not reliably repair the constraint (validity is not monotone in window size), the two-pointer shrink is unsound and a different tool is needed.
members: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
Longest Subarray With Diff At Most Limit

families.name: Shrink-while-valid: shortest covering window
families.idea: Grow the window until it satisfies the covering requirement, then shrink from the left for as long as it still does, recording the smallest valid size seen. Each left position is visited once, so the minimum window costs one pass.
signals: asks for the minimum-length window that contains or covers something
requirement reads like 'contains all characters of t' or 'sum at least target'
adding elements only helps, removing only hurts
families.trap: When order inside the window matters (covering a subsequence, not a multiset), frequency counting silently fails - you need a forward-match then backward-shrink scan instead.

families.name: Fixed-length window: slide and patch the summary
families.idea: The problem dictates the window length, so slide it one position at a time and patch a running summary (sum, hash, frequency table) by subtracting the outgoing element and adding the incoming one, never recomputing from scratch.
signals: the statement fixes the window length: 'of length k', 'k consecutive days', 'a permutation/anagram of p'
answer is the best, first, or all windows of exactly that size
the per-window quantity is rebuildable by removing one element and adding one
families.trap: Recomputing each window from scratch turns O(n) into O(n*k); and when the summary cannot be un-updated (like a max), a plain counter is not enough and a monotonic deque takes over.
members: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
Substring with Concatenation of All Words

families.name: Counting windows: at-most and leftmost-valid
families.idea: To count qualifying subarrays instead of finding one, note that every valid window ending at r contributes a whole run of left endpoints: sum window lengths to count 'at most K', get 'exactly K' as atMost(K) - atMost(K-1), and count 'at least' from the leftmost position where the window turns valid.
signals: asks for the NUMBER of subarrays/substrings meeting a condition, not the best one
condition is phrased with 'exactly k', 'at most', 'less than', or 'contains at least'
the count can be huge, so you are summing per-right-endpoint contributions
families.trap: Sliding a single window and counting it once per position undercounts; 'exactly K' is not a monotone window condition and must be decomposed into two at-most passes or a leftmost-valid count.
members: Count Subarrays With Score Less Than K
Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
Count Substrings With K-Frequency Characters II

families.name: Sort by start, sweep, coalesce
families.idea: Sort intervals by start and walk them once, comparing each new start against the running end: overlap extends the current merged block, a gap closes it. Unions, gaps, free time, and coverage are all read off this one sweep.
signals: input is a list of [start, end] pairs and the question is about overlap, union, gaps, or coverage
words like 'merge', 'non-overlapping', 'covered', 'free time', 'days without meetings'
the answer is itself a set of disjoint intervals or a measure of what they leave uncovered
families.trap: Skipping the sort, or only comparing adjacent pairs, misses that one long interval can swallow several later ones - always compare against the running maximum end, not the previous interval.

families.name: Timeline sweep: how many are active now
families.idea: Convert intervals into start and end events and sweep the timeline in order, maintaining the set or count of currently active intervals - typically a min-heap keyed by end time that pops everything already expired before each decision.
signals: asks for the minimum number of rooms/vehicles/machines, or peak simultaneous load
wording like 'at any moment', 'simultaneously', 'can everyone fit'
queries ask about whichever intervals are alive at a given point in time
families.trap: Greedily binding each interval to a fixed resource up front gives wrong minima - the true answer is the peak count of simultaneously active intervals, which only the ordered sweep exposes.
members: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query

families.name: Two-heap partition: the needed element stays on top
families.idea: Split the elements into two heaps chosen so the item you will need next is always a heap top - classically a max-heap of the lower half facing a min-heap of the upper half, rebalanced so their sizes differ by at most one, which makes the median an O(1) read.
signals: asks for a running median, or repeated access to the boundary between the small half and the large half
elements arrive one at a time and every insertion must stay cheap
the pool splits into two classes and you always consume the best of a specific class
families.trap: One heap or a re-sort makes each query linear; and if elements can also leave (a sliding window), plain heaps are not enough - you need lazy deletion and careful rebalancing.
members: Find Median from a Data Stream
Largest Number After Digit Swaps by Parity

families.name: Locked heap feeds available heap as the threshold advances
families.idea: Hold items locked in one heap keyed by the requirement that unlocks them (capital needed, release time); as the budget or clock advances, migrate everything newly unlocked into a second heap keyed by desirability, then greedily take that heap's top.
signals: each item has a prerequisite (cost, start time) plus a value, and you repeatedly pick the best currently-available one
resources free up over time and get reassigned (rooms, machines, chairs)
wording like 'maximize after k picks' or 'assign to the smallest free ...'
families.trap: Rescanning all items for the best affordable one each round is quadratic, and releasing only one unlocked item per step misses that a single advance of the threshold can unlock many at once.
members: The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Chair

families.name: Greedy loop: pop the extreme, transform, push back
families.idea: A priority queue drives a greedy simulation: pop the current extreme element, apply the operation to it, and push the transformed result back until the process ends. Correctness rests on an exchange argument - acting on the extreme element first is always safe.
signals: repeatedly combine or consume the smallest/largest elements of a shrinking-growing pool
each operation changes an element's key and the element re-enters the pool
asks for minimum total cost or the best arrangement after many rounds
families.trap: The greedy choice needs justification, and stepping the simulation forward one operation at a time can blow up - sometimes only running it backwards or batching steps with a modulo finishes in time.
members: Construct Target Array with Multiple Sums

families.name: Frontier heap over k sorted sources
families.idea: Seed a min-heap with the first element of every sorted source; each pop yields the next-smallest element overall and pushes that same source's successor. The heap always holds exactly one frontier element per unfinished source, so total work is O(N log k).
signals: input is several already-sorted lists, arrays, or matrix rows to combine
asks for the fully merged output, or just the kth smallest across all sources
k sources but you only ever need the global minimum of their fronts
families.trap: Concatenating everything and re-sorting throws away the given order (O(N log N) instead of O(N log k)), and pushing entire lists into the heap instead of one frontier element per source defeats the point.
members: Kth Smallest Number in M Sorted Lists
Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix

families.name: Invisible sorted lists: merge a matrix you never build
families.idea: The sorted sources are not handed to you - combinations (pair sums, fractions, prime multiples) form a virtual matrix whose rows are sorted. Merge it lazily: seed the heap with each row's first cell, and on every pop push that cell's successors, never materializing the grid.
signals: asks for the k smallest sums, products, or fractions formed by combining sorted arrays
the full combination space is quadratic or infinite, but k is small
a sequence is defined by multiplying earlier answers by fixed factors
families.trap: Generating and sorting all combinations is O(n^2 log n) and times out; and without a visited set or dedup on pop, the same virtual cell enters the heap through multiple predecessors.
members: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums

families.name: Boundary search on sorted indexes
families.idea: The array defines a yes/no test that is false up to some index and true from there on; binary search finds that flip point. Exact lookups, insert positions, and first/last occurrences are all the same flip-point question asked slightly differently.
signals: sorted array with O(log n) expected
find the first or last position where a condition holds
an API or array answers a monotone yes/no question per index
families.trap: Off-by-one drift: returning mid the moment it satisfies the test instead of tightening toward the boundary, so equal runs or absent targets resolve to the wrong side.
members: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array

families.name: Halving by structural test, not value comparison
families.idea: The array is not plainly sorted, so comparing mid against a target proves nothing. Instead a structural check at mid — which half is sorted, which neighbor is larger, whether pair-parity is intact — proves which half must contain the answer, so you can still discard half each step.
signals: sorted array rotated an unknown number of times
find a peak, minimum, or odd-one-out with no target value given
a local comparison at any index points toward the half holding the answer
families.trap: Duplicates can make both halves look identical at mid; then neither half can be safely discarded and the worst case degrades toward linear time.
members: Single Element in a Sorted Array
Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II

families.name: Binary search on the answer space
families.idea: The unknown is a number — a speed, capacity, distance, or value — where feasibility is monotone: once one candidate works, everything on one side of it works too. Binary search the candidate range and write a greedy or counting check that tests a single guess.
signals: minimize the maximum, or maximize the minimum
smallest speed, capacity, or time so a constraint still holds
k-th smallest value where counting items at most x is cheap
checking one candidate is easy but computing the best directly is hard
families.trap: Reaching for DP or greedy over the array itself; the monotone quantity is the answer, not the array, and the array is only ever scanned inside the feasibility check.
members: Maximum Running Time of N Computers
Maximum Value at a Given Index in a Bounded Array
Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
Kth Smallest Product of Two Sorted Arrays

families.name: Counting through sorted positions
families.idea: Once the data is sorted, 'how many satisfy the condition' stops being a scan and becomes a boundary lookup: the count is just an index. The final answer is small arithmetic over one or two such counts.
signals: count elements, pairs, or rows meeting a threshold
many queries asked against the same static data
answer decomposes into counts, like things started minus things ended
families.trap: Answering every query with a fresh linear scan; the whole point is that one sort turns each count into an O(log n) position lookup.
members: Count Pairs Whose Sum is Less than Target
The K Weakest Rows in a Matrix
Number of Flowers in Full Bloom

families.name: Sorted prefix sums answer budget queries
families.idea: Sort the costs and precompute prefix sums; then any 'how much fits under this budget' or 'what does this choice cost in total' question collapses to one binary search plus O(1) prefix arithmetic.
signals: maximize how many items fit under a sum limit
total cost of raising or lowering everything to a chosen value
many independent queries over the same collection of costs
families.trap: Recomputing sums from scratch per query or per candidate — without prefix sums the binary search saves nothing — and letting large prefix totals overflow.
members: Minimum Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal
Sum of Mutated Array Closest to Target
Maximum Number of Integers to Choose from a Range I

families.name: Search the value, verify with a sweep
families.idea: The candidates form a numeric range far too large to enumerate pair by pair, but sorted data lets one linear or two-pointer sweep test any single candidate. Binary search the value and use the sweep as the monotone yes/no oracle.
signals: k-th smallest among O(n^2) implicit pairs or subarray sums
place or choose items to maximize the minimum spacing
candidate range is huge but any one candidate is cheap to test against sorted data
families.trap: Materializing all pairs or subarray sums up front — that O(n^2) enumeration is exactly the cost the value search exists to avoid.
members: Range Sum of Sorted Subarray Sums

families.name: Sort so valid partners form a contiguous range
families.idea: When a pair condition depends only on the values, sorting makes every anchor's valid partners occupy one contiguous stretch of the array, so two pointers or a single binary search per anchor replaces checking every pair.
signals: count or find pairs meeting a sum or difference threshold
the pair condition is symmetric in the two values, so original order is irrelevant
for each element, ask whether the other array holds a near or far enough neighbor
families.trap: Sorting anyway when the condition involves original indices — the positional information is destroyed and the count silently comes out wrong.
members: Find the Distance Value Between Two Arrays

families.name: Size-k heap: keep only the k best
families.idea: Hold the k best items seen so far in a heap whose root is the weakest of them; each new item either loses to the root and is discarded, or replaces it. The heap never grows past k, so n items cost O(n log k) and the root is always the current k-th best.
signals: asks for the k largest / smallest / closest, not a fully sorted output
k is much smaller than n, or elements arrive as a stream
only the k winners matter; order among the losers is irrelevant
families.trap: Reaching for a full O(n log n) sort, or a max-heap of all n items, when a min-heap capped at k (or quickselect for a one-shot query) does strictly less work.
members: Kth Largest Element in an Array
Kth Largest Element in a Stream
Find the Kth Largest Integer in the Array
Find Subsequence of Length K with the Largest Sum
Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers

families.name: k rounds of pop, mutate, push back
families.idea: When each of k operations should touch the current extreme element, a heap serves it in O(log n): pop the top, apply the operation, push the changed value back. The heap reorders itself, so the next round again sees the true extreme.
signals: 'perform k operations' where each operation changes exactly one element
the best move is always on the current maximum or minimum
a modified element stays in play and can be picked again later
families.trap: Sorting once up front breaks after the first mutation - the changed element may no longer belong where it was, and order must be restored after every step, which is exactly what the heap amortizes.
members: Maximal Score After Applying K Operations
Final Array State After K Multiplication Operations I

families.name: Count first, then rank by frequency
families.idea: The values stop mattering once you tally them: build a count map, then run the usual top-k machinery (heap or buckets) over the counts. Every decision - keep, drop, schedule next - is made on frequency, never on the raw value.
signals: 'most frequent' or 'least frequent' language in the ask
keeping or removing elements is judged by how often they occur
the answer would survive relabeling all the actual values
families.trap: Working on the raw elements instead of their counts; and when deleting, missing that removing the rarest values first is what minimizes the distinct survivors.
members: Least Number of Unique Integers after K Removals

families.name: Heap as a frontier over a huge candidate space
families.idea: When the candidates (pairs, sums, positions across lists) are far too many to enumerate, keep a small heap holding just a frontier - a set guaranteed to contain the next-best candidate. Pop the best, then push only its immediate successors.
signals: k-th best over combinations drawn from two or more arrays or lists
the candidate space is combinatorial (n^2 pairs, 2^n subsets) but only k answers are needed
each candidate has one or two natural successor candidates derived from it
families.trap: Materializing every combination first - all n^2 pair sums or all subset sums - when the frontier never needs to hold more than about O(k) or one entry per list at a time.
members: K Maximum Sum Combinations From Two Arrays
Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
Find the K-Sum of an Array

families.name: Cancel against the stack top
families.idea: The stack holds the still-unresolved prefix, and each incoming symbol is checked against only the top, because in nested or adjacent structures the newest unresolved item is the only one it can legally close or erase. Match means pop; otherwise push and wait.
signals: symbols that open and close in pairs, or adjacent equals that annihilate
each removal exposes a new adjacency that may cascade into further removals
validity or cleanup questions about brackets and repeated deletions
families.trap: Re-scanning the string to apply removals until nothing changes - quadratic - when one left-to-right pass with a stack absorbs every cascade automatically.
members: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
Minimum String Length After Removing Substrings
Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses

families.name: Monotonic stack: wait for your resolver
families.idea: Keep the stack ordered so that every element on it is still waiting for the first future element that beats it. Each new arrival pops everything it resolves - recording an answer or an eviction at pop time - and then joins the queue of waiters. Every index is pushed and popped once, so the whole pass is linear.
signals: 'next / previous greater or smaller' phrasing, or a distance to it (days to wait, people seen)
each element's answer is decided by the first dominating element in one direction
counting or measuring spans that end at the nearest smaller or larger value
families.trap: Scanning forward from every element to find its resolver - O(n^2) on near-sorted input - instead of letting a single pass amortize all the waiting.
members: Number of Visible People in a Queue

families.name: Frame stack: save context on open, merge on close
families.idea: Nested input is evaluated with a stack of frames: on an opening token, push the partial result you were building and start fresh; on the matching close, pop the saved context and fold the inner result into it. It is recursion written by hand, with the call stack made explicit.
signals: nesting that repeats or transforms its inner content (k[...], parenthesized sub-expressions)
evaluating or expanding a small expression grammar
an inner result must be combined with a suspended outer computation
families.trap: Splitting on delimiters found by string search - same-kind brackets nest, so naive matching pairs the wrong ones; the stack pairs each close with its nearest open for free.

families.name: Hash map plus order structure, kept in sync
families.idea: No single container gives O(1) lookup and O(1) ordered maintenance at once, so compose two: a hash map to reach any entry instantly, and a second structure (array with swap-to-end, doubly linked list, frequency buckets) that owns the required ordering. Every operation updates both so neither goes stale.
signals: several operations that must each run in O(1) on the same data
needs lookup by key AND an ordering notion - recency, frequency, randomness, maximum
'design a structure' with eviction rules or a get-the-extreme operation
families.trap: Serving every operation from one structure - a plain map makes evict-least-recent a full scan; the fix is a second synchronized structure, not a cleverer single one.

families.name: Organize at write time, look up at read time
families.idea: Shift the work to writes: record each key's history or positions in the sorted order they naturally arrive in (timestamps, snapshot ids, word indices, prefix sums). Reads then never scan - they binary-search or directly index the prepared arrays.
signals: queries reference a past version, a timestamp, or a fixed range
many reads against data that only appends or never changes
'get the value as of X' rather than only the latest value
families.trap: Copying the whole structure at every snapshot or version - memory and write cost explode - when appending one (version, value) pair per actual change is enough.

families.name: Carry the aggregate with every update
families.idea: To answer an aggregate query (minimum, average, trimmed mean) in O(1), never compute it on demand - maintain it incrementally, adjusting stored state by exactly what each insertion or removal changes.
signals: the structure must report min / average / sum instantly at any moment
elements both enter and leave (push and pop, a sliding window) between queries
each update changes the aggregate by a delta you can compute locally
families.trap: Keeping one global aggregate that cannot be rolled back when its contributing element leaves - the fix is per-entry or per-bucket state (min-so-far on each node, balanced multisets), not rescanning.

families.name: 1D recurrence: answer at i from a few earlier answers
families.idea: Order positions 0..n and express the answer at each position purely from a small set of already-computed earlier positions (usually i-1 and i-2). The whole problem collapses to filling one array left to right.
signals: count ways / min cost to reach step n taking small fixed moves
each state depends only on one or two immediately earlier states
input is a line of items and the choice at i only interacts with nearby indices
families.trap: Plain recursion without memoization explodes exponentially, and when the allowed move depends on how you arrived (Frog Jump), the index alone stops being a sufficient state.

families.name: Knapsack: take-or-skip against a budget
families.idea: State is (items considered so far, remaining budget or target); each item is either skipped or taken, which shrinks the budget. Whether an item may repeat only changes the loop order — the table shape stays the same.
signals: pick a subset of items to hit or optimize an exact total or capacity
'can we make sum T' or 'fewest/most items making T'
each item usable once versus unlimited times
families.trap: Greedy by value or largest-coin-first fails on non-canonical inputs — coins {1,3,4} with target 6 break the largest-first instinct that works for real currency.

families.name: Two-string alignment over prefix pairs
families.idea: dp[i][j] answers the question for the first i characters of one string versus the first j of the other; the transition compares the two current characters and steps one or both prefixes back. Every member is the same table with a different cell formula.
signals: two strings compared as wholes: common subsequence, minimum edits, counted embeddings
answer for (i, j) built from (i-1, j), (i, j-1) and (i-1, j-1)
asked for a length, a distance, or a count over all interleavings of two sequences
families.trap: Two greedy pointers matching characters as early as possible looks right but is not optimal — a deferred match can preserve strictly more options later.

families.name: Boolean prefix-pair matching (wildcards and interleaving)
families.idea: dp[i][j] holds a yes/no: can prefix i of the source satisfy prefix j of the pattern (or can prefixes of two sources weave into the target)? Special symbols like '*' make a single cell depend on several earlier cells at once.
signals: does a string match a pattern containing * or ? semantics
can two sequences merge into a third while each keeps its internal order
a feasibility (true/false) answer over prefixes rather than an optimized quantity
families.trap: Backtracking over every '*' expansion blows up exponentially on adversarial inputs like long runs of a's; the prefix table caps the work at O(n*m).

families.name: Grid DP: cell from its already-solved neighbors
families.idea: Sweep the grid in an order where each cell's dependencies (above/left, or below/right) are already final, then combine them with the cell's own cost. Picking the sweep direction — and knowing when it must be reversed — is the whole trick.
signals: path from one corner to another moving only right/down
each cell's best value is determined by adjacent cells' best values
triangle or pyramid rows where entry i is fed by entries i-1 and i of the row above
families.trap: Dungeon Game breaks the forward sweep: minimum starting health must be computed backwards from the exit, because a forward pass cannot know how much future rooms will demand.

families.name: Prefix segmentation: cut the sequence into valid chunks
families.idea: dp[i] asks whether (or in how many ways) the first i characters split into valid pieces; the transition tries every legal last chunk ending at i. The only thing that changes between members is what counts as a valid chunk.
signals: split a string into dictionary words or valid codes
count the decodings or segmentations of a sequence
the answer for a prefix is assembled from shorter prefixes plus one final chunk
families.trap: Enumerating all segmentations up front — feasibility (Word Break) is polynomial, but full reconstruction (Word Break II) can be exponential, so verify the dp says 'possible' before rebuilding paths.

families.name: Best run ending at each position
families.idea: Anchor the subproblem at the element that ends the run: for each position compute the best subarray or chain finishing exactly there, by extending an earlier run or starting fresh. The final answer is the best over all anchors.
signals: best contiguous product/sum where optimal substructure only holds if you fix the last element
longest increasing chain, possibly with a count of how many achieve it
extend-or-restart choice at every element
families.trap: Tracking only the maximum ending here fails with negatives — a large negative product flips into the new maximum at the next negative number, so the minimum must ride along beside it.
members: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix

families.name: Farthest-reach frontier
families.idea: Sweep left to right maintaining the farthest index currently reachable; you never commit to a specific path, only grow the frontier. Minimum steps falls out by counting how many times the frontier window rolls over.
signals: array values are maximum step sizes and the question is reachability or fewest jumps
minimum boosts/refuels to cover a distance, choosing among options passed along the way
families.trap: Simulating concrete jump sequences or running DP over positions costs O(n^2); the frontier argument shows only the running maximum reach ever matters.

families.name: Sort, then match the extremes
families.idea: Sort by the quantity that measures how much the choice matters, then pair or assign greedily from the ends; an exchange argument shows any optimal solution can be rewritten, swap by swap, into the sorted matching without getting worse.
signals: pair items under a capacity: two per boat, smallest sufficient cookie per child
split items into two groups where the per-item cost difference is what matters
transfer or swap elements between two collections at minimum total cost
families.trap: Sorting by a raw value instead of the decision's delta — Two City Scheduling needs ordering by costA minus costB, not by either cost alone.

families.name: Build the extreme number, most significant digit first
families.idea: An improvement at a more significant position beats any change made after it, so decide digits left to right: at each position keep or place the best digit available under the problem's constraint — a budget of deletions, a single swap, a palindrome mirror.
signals: largest/smallest number after removing k digits or performing one swap
arrange or concatenate pieces so the resulting number is maximal
leading-zero and digit-count constraints on the constructed answer
families.trap: Comparing candidate pieces numerically — Largest Number requires the concatenation test (a+b versus b+a), and forgetting leading-zero rules corrupts an otherwise-correct greedy answer.

families.name: One-pass sweep with a running ledger
families.idea: Walk the array once keeping a tiny running ledger — fuel surplus, profit delta, eligibility of the current slot — and commit each local decision immediately; when the ledger goes negative it also tells you exactly where the next viable attempt begins.
signals: circular route feasibility with a gain and a cost at every stop
total profit equals the sum of every upward move when you may transact freely
place or accept items subject only to immediate-neighbor conditions
families.trap: When the constraint looks both left and right (Candy), a single forward pass cannot satisfy it — you need a second sweep in the opposite direction and the max of both.
members: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II

families.name: Cheapest path when edges have costs
families.idea: When edges carry costs, plain BFS order lies: the frontier must expand in order of accumulated cost, settling each node the first time it is popped from a priority queue (Dijkstra).
signals: edges have weights, times, costs, or probabilities
asks for minimum total cost / time (or maximum probability) to reach a target
moving between cells or nodes has non-uniform price
families.trap: BFS by hop count picks a path with fewer edges but higher total cost; conversely Dijkstra's settled-once guarantee breaks if anything behaves like a negative weight.
members: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid

families.name: BFS over augmented states
families.idea: The queue entry is not just a position but position plus extra memory (a visited bitmask, a remaining budget, the route you are riding); shortest path in that enlarged state graph answers questions a plain position-BFS cannot.
signals: fewest steps, but position alone does not determine which moves are legal
a small budget, key set, or subset of targets must be tracked along the way
the same cell can be worth revisiting under different conditions
families.trap: Marking a bare cell or node as visited prunes states that differ only in the hidden component, silently discarding the optimal path.
members: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination

families.name: Detecting and measuring cycles
families.idea: A traversal that reaches an already-seen node has closed a cycle; whether you only need to notice this (tree check) or measure the loop (shortest or longest cycle) decides how much bookkeeping the visit stamps must carry.
signals: is this graph a tree / connected with no loops
find the shortest or longest cycle in the graph
a repeated visit or extra edge is the anomaly being asked about
families.trap: In an undirected graph the edge straight back to your parent looks like a cycle; forgetting to exclude it reports loops that do not exist.

families.name: Answers from degrees, not traversal
families.idea: Some graph questions never need a walk: one counting pass over the edge list or matrix (in/out degree, per-row or per-column aggregate) already identifies the special node, because the property asked about is local arithmetic.
signals: find the node everyone points to but that points at nobody
the property is about counts of relationships, not about paths
a single pass over the pairs or the matrix feels like it should suffice
families.trap: Building adjacency lists and traversing works but hides the O(edges) counting solution and makes tie cases (two candidates) easier to get wrong.

families.name: Kahn's peeling of prerequisite DAGs
families.idea: Items with unmet prerequisites wait; repeatedly emitting anything whose in-degree has dropped to zero produces a valid order, and finishing with items still waiting proves a circular dependency.
signals: ordering constrained by prerequisites / dependency edges
asks 'can all tasks be finished' or 'return any valid order'
completing one item unlocks others
families.trap: Detecting the cycle with DFS but only a plain visited set: without an on-stack (three-color) mark, a cross edge to a finished node is mistaken for a cycle.
members: Find All Possible Recipes from Given Supplies
Sort Items by Groups Respecting Dependencies

families.name: Recover an unknown ordering from evidence
families.idea: The ordering itself is the unknown: each piece of evidence (a pair of adjacent sorted words, a pairwise condition) contributes one 'x before y' edge, and topologically sorting the constraint graph reconstructs a consistent arrangement or proves none exists.
signals: a custom alphabet or hidden ranking must be deduced
the input is claimed to be sorted under unknown rules
many pairwise 'this before that' conditions must all hold at once
families.trap: Comparing whole words instead of only the first differing character, and missing the invalid case where a word appears after one of its own prefixes.

families.name: Longest chain through a DAG
families.idea: With unlimited parallelism the minimum total time equals the longest dependency chain: process nodes in topological order and give each one the best value over its prerequisites plus its own cost.
signals: minimum semesters / months when independent tasks can run in parallel
each item waits only for its own prerequisites to finish
asks for the longest path or chain through a dependency structure
families.trap: Counting BFS layers works only while every task takes equal time; with durations the answer follows the critical path, not the number of levels.
members: Longest Path With Different Adjacent Characters

families.name: Grid cells as mergeable regions
families.idea: Treat each cell (or cell fragment) as its own set and union neighbors that belong together; region counts and sizes then fall out of the merge bookkeeping instead of a fresh traversal per query.
signals: count islands / regions / enclosed areas in a grid
cells connect to orthogonal neighbors of the same kind
the grid mutates over time and the count is needed after every change
families.trap: Re-flood-filling after every mutation is quadratic, and a newly added cell can join several existing regions at once: the count rises by one, then falls once per distinct neighbor root.
members: Last Day Where You Can Still Cross

families.name: Merge records that share a key
families.idea: Two records belong to one group whenever they share an attribute (an email, a row or column, a neighboring value, near-identical spelling); union on every shared attribute and the final components are exactly the groups.
signals: merge accounts or group items that share any common element
same row / same column / consecutive value connects two items
the answer is the number of groups or the size of the largest one
families.trap: Comparing all record pairs to find shared keys is O(n^2); map each attribute to its first owner and union newcomers against that owner instead.
members: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column

families.name: Edge-at-a-time cycle gate
families.idea: Feed edges through one at a time: if both endpoints already share a root the edge would close a cycle (reject or report it), otherwise union them. Sorting the edges by cost turns the very same gate into Kruskal's minimum spanning tree.
signals: find the edge whose removal turns the graph back into a tree
just asks whether two nodes are connected
connect everything at minimum total cost
families.trap: Without union by size and path compression the find chains degrade to O(n); and cost problems with a build-your-own option need a virtual node so self-supply becomes an ordinary edge.
members: Find if Path Exists in Graph
Optimize Water Distribution in a Village

families.name: Shared-prefix paths with per-node payload
families.idea: Every root-to-node path is a prefix shared by all words below it, so walking a query letter by letter visits exactly its prefixes; the whole design decision is what to cache at each node (end flags, counts, sums, best suggestions).
signals: many words with repeated prefix lookups
autocomplete or suggestions after each typed character
sum or count over all stored keys starting with a given prefix
families.trap: A node being reachable is not the same as a word ending there; dropping the end-of-word flag conflates prefixes with actual members.
members: Check If a Word is a Prefix of Any Word in a Sentence

families.name: One trie matches many words at once
families.idea: Load the whole dictionary into a trie so a single walk over the text, grid, or query advances through every candidate word simultaneously; a mismatch at one node prunes all words below it in a single step.
signals: find which of many dictionary words occur in a text or letter grid
replace tokens with their shortest dictionary root
lookups must support wildcards against a stored word set
families.trap: Scanning the text once per dictionary word multiplies the work by the word count; and in grid search, forgetting to remove found words re-reports duplicates and destroys the pruning.
members: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

families.name: Preorder walk equals sorted order
families.idea: If a trie's children are visited in key order, its preorder traversal enumerates all stored keys lexicographically; decimal numbers form an implicit 10-way trie, so dictionary order over a numeric range needs no explicit tree at all.
signals: output required in lexicographical / dictionary order
k-th smallest in dictionary order over a numeric range
ties among equal items broken alphabetically
families.trap: Materializing and sorting every candidate as strings cannot skip anything; k-th queries need subtree-size counting to leap over whole prefixes instead of stepping item by item.

families.name: Post-order aggregation with a global best
families.idea: Each call returns a compact summary of its subtree (usually a height or best downward value); the parent combines the two child summaries, and any answer that bends through a node is recorded in a variable outside the recursion. The value you return is deliberately not the value you are optimizing.
signals: asks for a longest path, largest sum, or widest span measured anywhere in the tree, not just from the root
the best answer may pass through a node, joining its left and right sides
the answer at a node can be written using only numbers computed from its children
families.trap: Returning the through-node answer to the parent — a path that already bends through both children cannot be extended upward, so the recursion must hand back the one-sided value only.
members: Height of Binary Tree After Subtree Removal Queries

families.name: BST ordering as a sorted stream
families.idea: An in-order walk of a BST visits keys in ascending order, so questions about ranks, neighbors, or ordering validity become questions about a sorted sequence you can stream one node at a time — or answer by pruning to the single child that could contain the target.
signals: the tree is a BST and the statement mentions kth, closest, successor, or checking the ordering itself
comparing each visited value to the previously visited one would settle the question
at every node, one comparison against the node's value rules out an entire subtree
families.trap: Validating each node only against its immediate children — a node deep in the left subtree must still be smaller than the root, so the constraint is a running range (or the previous in-order value), not a local parent-child check.
members: Kth Smallest Element in a BST

families.name: Rebuilding a tree from traversal order
families.idea: One traversal sequence plus one extra piece of structure — null markers, an in-order companion, explicit depths, or a sortedness guarantee — pins the tree down uniquely. Consume the sequence left to right with a shared cursor: the current element becomes the root, and recursion claims the run of elements belonging to each subtree.
signals: input is a flat sequence (array or string) and output is a tree, or the reverse
the statement names a traversal order: preorder, inorder, or sorted
each recursive call naturally owns one contiguous run of the sequence
families.trap: Recomputing subtree boundaries by slicing or scanning at every level — a single advancing index, plus a lookup or depth check to know when to stop, rebuilds the tree in one pass.
members: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
Build Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
Recover a Tree From Preorder Traversal

families.name: Return the rewritten subtree
families.idea: The recursion's return value is a transformed (possibly deleted) subtree, and the parent finishes its own transformation by reattaching whatever came back. Working bottom-up means every child is already in final form when the parent rewires its pointers.
signals: the task changes the tree's shape: mirror it, flatten it, or remove nodes from it
a node's new children can be written as an expression over its transformed old children
the natural function signature is node in, node out
families.trap: Overwriting child pointers before recursing into them — transform (or save) the original left and right first, otherwise you walk pointers you have already redirected.
members: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List

families.name: Accumulator threaded down the path
families.idea: State that depends only on the root-to-current-node path — a remaining total, the current depth — travels downward as an argument, and decisions fire at leaves or on first arrival at a depth. Nothing needs to flow back up except the final answer.
signals: the question is about root-to-leaf paths, or about the first or deepest node at some depth
what matters at a node depends on its ancestors, never on its siblings
depth or a running total appears naturally as one extra parameter
families.trap: Testing the target at internal nodes — a root-to-leaf condition may only be checked where both children are absent, or nodes with a single child produce false positives.

families.name: Drain the queue one level at a time
families.idea: Freeze the queue's size before the inner loop and you process exactly one level per outer iteration; each level can then be aggregated, reversed, or linked as a unit before its children are enqueued. Recording the queue length at loop start is the entire trick.
signals: output is organized by depth: a list per level, one value per level, or alternating direction
phrases like each level, level averages, zigzag, or next pointers between neighbors
a node needs to know its horizontal neighbor at the same depth
families.trap: Popping until the queue is empty mixes parents with freshly pushed children — the level boundary only exists if you capture the queue size before draining it.
members: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
Level Order Traversal of Binary Tree
Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
Connect All Siblings of a Binary Tree

families.name: BFS layers count minimum moves
families.idea: When every move costs the same, breadth-first exploration visits states in order of distance from the start, so the layer where a state first appears is its minimum number of moves. The graph is often implicit: neighbors are generated on the fly and a visited set prevents re-expansion.
signals: asks for the minimum number of steps or transformations to reach a target
each state has a small set of one-step neighbors you can generate: change one letter, turn one wheel, step to an adjacent cell
every move is equally expensive — no weights anywhere in the statement
families.trap: Reaching for DFS — depth-first finds a path but not the shortest one, and forgetting to mark states visited at enqueue time floods the frontier with duplicates.

families.name: Place, check, undo on a constrained board
families.idea: Fill positions one at a time, testing each candidate against constraints created by earlier placements; on a dead end, erase the last placement and try the next candidate. Constant-time constraint checks — per-column, per-diagonal, per-box occupancy sets — are what make the search feasible.
signals: place items on a board so that no two conflict
conflicts run along rows, columns, diagonals, or boxes
the answer is a completed arrangement, all arrangements, or a count of them
families.trap: Re-scanning the board to test each candidate — without O(1) occupancy sets the check cost multiplies into the exponential search instead of staying outside it.

families.name: Grid DFS with mark and unmark
families.idea: Explore neighboring cells recursively, marking a cell on entry so one path never reuses it. If different candidate paths may need the same cell, the mark must be undone on the way out; if membership is permanent, as in filling a region, it must not be.
signals: trace a path or region through a 2D grid
moves go to orthogonally adjacent cells
a cell can belong to one candidate path but not another
families.trap: Confusing the two marking regimes — region-filling without a permanent mark recurses forever, while path-search without an undo wrongly blocks cells for sibling branches.

families.name: Cut a string into valid segments
families.idea: Choose where the next cut goes: try each feasible prefix length, validate that segment, and recurse on the remaining suffix, retracting the cut when the suffix cannot be completed. Validity may depend on the segment alone or on segments already committed.
signals: split or partition a string so that every piece satisfies a rule
a piece's validity can depend on earlier pieces: uniqueness, an arithmetic relation, a count limit
segment lengths are small and bounded, which keeps the branching factor tiny
families.trap: Leading zeros and missing bounds — a numeric segment like 05 passes a naive parse, and ignoring the small maximum segment length turns a tight search into a slow one.
members: Split a String Into the Max Number of Unique Substrings

families.name: Assign items to groups under a target
families.idea: Try each item in every group it could join, recursing after each tentative assignment and taking it back on failure. Pruning is the real content: sort items so large ones fail early, skip groups whose partial totals are identical, and cut the branch the moment a group overshoots.
signals: divide items into a fixed number of groups with equal or bounded totals
n is tiny, fifteen or so — a strong hint that exponential assignment search is intended
the goal is feasibility or a minimum number of operations, not listing every arrangement
families.trap: Trying an item in several currently-identical groups — without skipping equal-total buckets the search repeats the same partition once per group ordering.
members: Minimum Moves to Spread Stones Over Grid

families.name: Collect every source-to-target path
families.idea: Grow one shared path buffer while descending: append the current node, recurse into each neighbor, snapshot the buffer whenever the target or a leaf is reached, then pop on the way back so sibling branches start clean. Every complete path is emitted, not just one.
signals: the output is all paths or all sequences, so the answer is a list of lists
the structure is a tree or an acyclic graph, so no visited set is needed
each result is a copy of the current root-to-here trail
families.trap: Appending the live buffer to the results — without copying at emission time, every collected path later mutates into whatever the buffer ends as.
members: All Paths From Source to Target

families.name: Include-or-exclude per element
families.idea: Walk the elements once; at each one, branch into take-it and leave-it, so the leaves of the recursion tree enumerate every subset exactly once. Extra requirements — a sum target, duplicate elements, a per-character toggle — layer onto the same two-way decision as filters or branch skips.
signals: asks for all subsets or combinations, where order inside a pick does not matter
each element is used at most once, independently of the others
duplicates in the input mean identical outputs must be reported only once
families.trap: Handling duplicates by deduplicating finished results — sorting the input and skipping a repeated value at the same decision level prunes the doubled work instead of doing it and discarding it.

families.name: Build the output one slot at a time
families.idea: The output has positions, and recursion fills them left to right; the candidate set for each position comes from a rule — the letters mapped to the current digit, the unused remainder of a pool, or a balance condition. Each recursion level commits one position and undoes it after exploring.
signals: asks for all orderings or sequences, so the same elements in a different order count separately
the options at each position depend on what was already placed
a validity rule such as balance or remaining counts can reject a partial prefix early
families.trap: Pruning only at full length — an already-impossible prefix should be cut immediately, and duplicate letters need per-value counts rather than per-index used flags, or the same output is produced many times.
members: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number

families.name: Prefix state + hash of earlier states
families.idea: Any subarray condition that can be rewritten as prefix[j] minus prefix[i] hitting a target becomes a single left-to-right pass: carry a running prefix state and a map of states already seen, and at each step ask how many times (or how early) a matching earlier state occurred.
signals: count subarrays whose sum hits an exact target
longest subarray with a zero or equal balance after remapping values
subarray sum divisible by k, or a parity condition over the prefix
the condition is about a contiguous range but values can be negative or non-monotone
families.trap: Reaching for a sliding window — negatives, zero-remapping, and parity states destroy the monotonicity a window needs; and forgetting to seed the map with the empty prefix (state 0 before index 0) silently drops every subarray that starts at the beginning.

families.name: Canonical form as hash key
families.idea: Design a normalization that erases exactly the differences the problem declares irrelevant — letter identity, absolute position, precise spelling — so every equivalent object collapses to the same key, and testing equivalence or grouping becomes plain hash lookup.
signals: are two things 'the same' up to renaming or translation
group or count distinct shapes, files, or structures
match queries against a dictionary under increasingly forgiving rules
families.trap: A signature that is not truly canonical — mapping consistently in one direction while two different characters collide in the other, or recording a shape by raw coordinates instead of anchoring it to a fixed origin cell.

families.name: Hash set as O(1) membership oracle
families.idea: Load one collection into a set (or count map) so 'have I seen this?' costs O(1); then scan the other collection — or generate candidates — and test each against it, getting deduplication and intersection for free.
signals: which elements appear in both collections
does some element exist, repeat, or stand out
enumerate candidate values and report only the distinct ones
families.trap: Using a plain set when multiplicity matters — duplicates silently collapse and intersection counts come out wrong; a count map you decrement per match is the multiset version of the same oracle.

families.name: Index once, answer queries by lookup
families.idea: Split the work into two phases: one pass builds a key-to-answer (or rank, or bucket) table from the reference data, then the main loop resolves each item with a single lookup instead of rescanning the reference — turning O(n times q) into O(n plus q).
signals: queries asked against a fixed reference array or string
a custom ordering or priority defined by another sequence
sparse data where only the stored entries matter
records must be joined on a shared key field
families.trap: Re-scanning the reference for every query because the loop reads naturally that way — the map exists precisely to delete that inner scan; for sparse structures, iterating the full logical length instead of only the stored keys throws the savings away.
members: Dot Product of Two Sparse Vectors

families.name: Per-key position memory
families.idea: Store, for each key, the position or time it was first (or last) seen; comparing the current index against that remembered position is what detects a cycle, enforces a cooldown, or measures a per-key gap — a boolean 'seen' flag cannot answer any of those.
signals: a decimal or state sequence eventually repeats and you must locate where the cycle starts
suppress or allow events per key within a time window
each element's contribution depends on how far back the same key last appeared
families.trap: Storing that a key was seen instead of where — you can detect that a repeat happened but you cannot mark the cycle start or compute the gap the answer actually needs.

families.name: Frequency vector as the object
families.idea: When order is irrelevant, a string or collection is fully described by its count vector; equality, containment, grouping, and even permutation counting all become cheap operations on those small fixed-size vectors instead of on the data itself.
signals: is one string a rearrangement of another
can you build X from the letters of Y
group words that are rearrangements of each other
find every window that is a rearrangement of a pattern
families.trap: Sorting the strings for every comparison — O(n log n) where a 26-slot count array is O(n); and in windowed versions, rebuilding counts for each window instead of updating one character in and one character out.
members: Find Words That Can Be Formed by Characters
Find All Anagrams in a String
Check if One String Swap Can Make Strings Equal

families.name: Palindromes from paired counts
families.idea: A palindrome is mirrored pairs around at most one unpaired center, so you never construct one — count each unit, greedily take complete pairs, and reserve the single allowed odd (or self-mirrored) unit for the middle.
signals: can these letters be rearranged into a palindrome
longest palindrome buildable from given letters or words
the answer depends only on how many matching pairs you can form
families.trap: Trying to build or enumerate actual palindromes; or forgetting the one legal center — at most one odd count is allowed, and a self-reversed unit can occupy the middle only once.
members: Longest Palindrome by Concatenating Two-Letter Words

families.name: One sweep, O(1) running summary
families.idea: Instead of re-scanning everything behind you at each index, maintain a constant-size running summary — left total, current run length, count of currently active operations — and each position's answer falls out of comparing that summary to a global total or to the previous run.
signals: a point where the left side balances the right side
longest streak of equal or qualifying values
count blocks formed where adjacent runs meet
many range updates applied before a single final read
families.trap: Recomputing a sum or streak from scratch at every index for O(n^2), or applying each range update element by element when a difference array plus one running sweep handles all of them in O(n + q).

families.name: Counts decide the order
families.idea: Count first, then let the counts — not the values — drive everything downstream: sort keys by their frequency, hand the cheapest slots to the most frequent items, or compare whole per-position tally vectors lexicographically.
signals: sort or rank by how often things occur
minimize total cost when frequent items should claim the cheap slots
rank candidates by votes tallied per position
most frequent element wins, with an explicit tiebreak rule
families.trap: Sorting by value and patching frequency in afterwards — the sort key must be built from the finished count table with the tiebreak encoded explicitly, or the greedy quietly hands a cheap slot to a rare item.
members: Minimum Number of Pushes to Type Word II

families.name: The answer lives in the count table
families.idea: One counting pass compresses the input into a small frequency table, and the question is then answered by reading the table itself — the first key with count one, whether the count values are pairwise distinct, or the overlap between two tables — rather than the original data.
signals: first or any element that appears exactly once
compare how often things occur across two inputs
a property of the frequencies themselves, not of the elements
families.trap: Trying to answer during the counting pass — the table is not trustworthy until the whole input is consumed, so the second pass (over the data or over the table) is not waste, it is the algorithm.
members: First Unique Character in a String

families.name: In-place transforms: don't clobber unread cells
families.idea: Rewriting a matrix in place means some cells are input and output at once. Either move values along closed swap cycles, or temporarily pack old and new state into the same cell and decode it in a second pass.
signals: 'in place' or O(1) extra space demanded for a matrix rewrite
a cell's new value depends on neighbors' OLD values
the transform permutes positions (rotate, transpose, reflect)
families.trap: Copying into a second matrix works but fails the space constraint, while naive in-place writing destroys values you still need to read.

families.name: Traversal orders as index bijections
families.idea: Any visiting order over a grid is a bijection between step number and (row, col). Implement it either as closed-form index arithmetic or as a walk with direction state plus boundary and turn rules.
signals: output is the grid's elements in an unusual order (spiral, diagonal, zigzag)
converting between a flat index and 2D coordinates
'fill the grid in this order' with nothing to optimize
families.trap: Writing four near-identical loops without shrinking the boundaries correctly - the last partial ring of an odd-sized or non-square grid is where these break.

families.name: Step-by-step grid simulation
families.idea: The grid encodes local movement rules, so you advance the state one tick at a time: track position and direction, check the blocking condition before each move, and stop on exit or on a repeated state.
signals: an object moves through a grid under stated local rules (falls, turns on walls, spreads)
asked where it ends up or how long it takes, not an optimum over choices
the environment itself can change while the object moves
families.trap: Hunting for a closed-form shortcut - the rules interact (a diverted ball, a spreading flood), so only faithful tick-by-tick simulation, sometimes interleaved with BFS, stays correct.
members: Number of Spaces Cleaning Robot Cleaned
Minimum Time Takes to Reach Destination Without Drowning

families.name: Monotone grids: search the answer, not the cells
families.idea: When rows and columns are sorted, or a yes/no property is monotone in some threshold, you can binary-search that threshold (or staircase-walk the boundary) and pay only a linear count or check per probe instead of enumerating every cell.
signals: rows and columns are sorted, or cell values grow with the index product
asked for a kth value, a boundary, or a minimum feasible threshold
the grid is too large to materialize or fully scan
families.trap: Flattening or heapifying the whole grid costs O(mn log mn) when a monotone predicate answers the same question in O((m+n) log range).
members: Kth Smallest Number in Multiplication Table
Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix

families.name: XOR cancellation: pairs annihilate
families.idea: Because x ^ x = 0 and XOR ignores order, anything contributing an even number of times vanishes from a running XOR. Equal prefix XORs mean the whole range between them cancels to zero, which turns range questions into pair-matching on prefixes.
signals: 'every element appears twice except one' phrasing
subarrays or ranges whose XOR must be zero or equal on both sides
tracking even/odd counts of a small alphabet through a stream
families.trap: The trick dies the moment duplicates come in threes or any other count - then you need per-bit counting modulo k, not one running XOR.
members: Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR
Find the Longest Substring Having Vowels in Even Counts

families.name: Bit surgery: isolate, clear, rebuild
families.idea: An integer is an array of bits you edit with shifts and masks: n & (n-1) deletes the lowest set bit, an all-ones mask of the right width flips a whole number, and shifting one bit at a time rebuilds a value in any order you choose.
signals: asked about the count, position, or pattern of set bits
'power of two' or 'exactly one bit set' phrasing
produce a complement, reversal, or mirror of a number's bits
families.trap: Width and sign bite: arithmetic shift on negatives, hidden 32-bit assumptions, and the n = 0 edge case all break naive mask code.

families.name: Flips are involutions: only parity matters
families.idea: A flip undoes itself, so each position's final state depends only on the parity of flips covering it, never on their order. Track that parity with a running counter or difference array instead of physically re-flipping anything.
signals: operations that toggle or invert bits, cells, or ranges
asked for the minimum number of operations to reach a target state
applying the same operation twice visibly cancels it
families.trap: Physically applying every flip costs O(nk); also greedy left-to-right is only valid because a position, once passed, can never be fixed by any later flip.
members: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
Minimum One Bit Operations to Make Integers Zero

families.name: Binary expansions as combinatorial addresses
families.idea: Map each object to a binary string so ranking, counting, and feasibility become arithmetic on bits: the kth object of a two-symbol language is (roughly) k written in binary, and popcount lower-bounds how many powers of two a sum needs.
signals: objects built from exactly two symbols or two choices per position
'find the kth such number' over a set that doubles per length
targets that must decompose into a given count of powers of two
families.trap: Generating and sorting the objects explicitly explodes exponentially - the binary index jumps straight to the answer without building the set.
members: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
Minimum Operations to Make the Integer Zero

families.name: Schoolbook addition with an explicit carry
families.idea: Big numbers arrive as digit containers (strings, arrays, linked lists) precisely because they overflow native integers. Walk the digits from the least significant end while maintaining a carry, and remember the leftover carry can mint a brand-new leading digit.
signals: numbers given as strings, digit arrays, or linked lists of digits
lengths in the thousands, or 'do not convert to integer' wording
add or increment semantics, possibly in an unusual base
families.trap: Parsing into a built-in integer overflows or is outright banned, and dropping the final carry after the loop silently loses the most significant digit.

families.name: The divmod loop: digits via % and /
families.idea: Repeated (n % base, n / base) peels digits off any integer, and the mirrored multiply-and-add rebuilds them. Reversal, palindrome tests, digit remapping, and base conversion are all the same loop with different bookkeeping.
signals: asked about a number's digits: their order, mirror image, or remapped shape
conversion to another base
'without converting to a string' hints
families.trap: The rebuilt number can overflow the integer type even when the input fits - guard before appending each digit, or only ever reverse half.

families.name: Cross product: one primitive for turns and lines
families.idea: For vectors AB and AC, the sign of the 2D cross product tells whether C lies left of, right of, or exactly on line AB. That single integer test powers collinearity checks, convexity scans, and hull construction with no slopes and no division.
signals: 'straight line' or 'same line' questions over integer points
convexity, turn direction, or fence/boundary phrasing
grouping many points by the line passing through them
families.trap: Computing slopes as dy/dx invites division-by-zero and float-precision bugs - vertical lines and duplicate points are exactly where slope-based code fails.
members: Check If It Is a Straight Line
Minimum Number of Lines to Cover Points

families.name: Axis-aligned rectangles: x and y are independent
families.idea: An axis-parallel rectangle is just two independent intervals, one per axis. Overlap is per-axis interval overlap, union area is inclusion-exclusion of those overlaps, and a rectangle exists in a point set exactly when its four corner coordinates co-occur.
signals: 'sides parallel to the axes' in the statement
overlap or union area of two rectangles
choosing points from a set to form a rectangle
families.trap: Treating edge-touching as overlap (or the reverse) - the strict-versus-non-strict inequality on each axis is the entire bug surface.
members: Maximum Area Rectangle With Point Constraints I

families.name: Pick the metric, stay in integers
families.idea: The movement or shape rule dictates the distance formula: squared Euclidean for circles (never take the root), Chebyshev max(|dx|, |dy|) when diagonal steps are allowed, Manhattan for axis-only steps. Each choice keeps every comparison in exact integer arithmetic.
signals: points inside a circle or within a radius
movement allowing diagonal steps, asked for travel time
maximize or minimize pairwise distances between grid points
families.trap: Calling sqrt introduces floating error and is never needed for comparisons; using Euclidean distance when movement is 8-directional overestimates travel time.
members: Queries on Number of Points Inside a Circle

families.name: gcd governs what is reachable
families.idea: Combining whole copies of two quantities by adding and subtracting can only ever produce multiples of their gcd (Bezout), and two repeating patterns align again at their lcm. Reachability and 'nth multiple of either' questions are gcd/lcm arithmetic, not search.
signals: two containers, strings, or step sizes combined by repetition
'can you measure exactly z' phrasing
nth number divisible by a or b, with n far too large to iterate
families.trap: State-space BFS passes the small cases, but the binding constraint is divisibility - if the target is not a multiple of the gcd, no sequence of moves will ever reach it.

families.name: Don't simulate: find the invariant
families.idea: The statement stages a long process - rounds of toggles, alternating turns, batches of tests - but a pairing or invariant argument collapses it to a closed form: divisors pair up, positions modulo k decide the game, and information capacity bounds what tests can distinguish.
signals: n up to 10^9 or beyond, yet the process reads step-by-step
repeated rounds, turns, or passes over the same objects
the answer is a single number with no construction requested
families.trap: Simulation times out by design; the real trap is not noticing the answer has a formula - count the process's fixed points instead of running it.
